verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline at the pinned (vulnerable) commit through a live Jenkins controller (JenkinsRule): the Pipeline steps exwsAllocate(path:), exwsAllocate(diskPoolId:) with a disk-pool workspace pattern expanded from build parameters, exwsAllocate(selectedRun:) replaying a workspace recorded by an earlier run, the injected exwsAllocate(subPath:), and the controller HTTP endpoints /exws/browse/{id}/ws/ and /exws/browse/{id}/cleanup. A build that supplies a value containing '..' reaches the agent-side join ExwsExecution.child(pathOnDisk) (or the controller join in the model actions) and works outside the disk's mount point. No network, GPU or GUI is needed: the workspace paths are temporary local directories and Jenkins' own Jetty test server.
sites: steps/ExwsAllocateExecution.java:219-243 computeCustomPath -- the reported site: only a relative-path and '${' check, then the path is stored as pathOnDisk (published fix adds the parent-segment check)

steps/ExwsAllocateExecution.java:265-301 computePathBasedOnTemplate -- the check runs on the raw pattern before replaceMacro expands build parameters; the expanded path is not checked (published fix adds the post-expansion check)

model/ExternalWorkspace.java:89-105 doWs -- the controller joins masterMountPoint and the recorded pathOnDisk and serves a DirectoryBrowserSupport with no containment (published fix adds it; package model, another package from the steps landing point)

steps/ExwsAllocateExecution.java:114-136 downstream branch -- a workspace recorded by an earlier run is taken from ExwsAllocateActionImpl and reused with no re-validation, then joined to the node mount point at steps/ExwsExecution.java:103-104 (real upstream code, untouched by the published fix)
steps/ExwsAllocateExecution.java:269-285 computeSubPath (injected) -- the default path is appended with a job-supplied sub-folder after only a relative-path check
model/ExternalWorkspace.java:107-124 doCleanup (injected) -- a POST action deletes the allocated workspace through getCompleteWorkspacePath() with no containment
routes: T0 (reported, real upstream): literal custom path '../outside' and 'sub/../../outside' in exwsAllocate path

T1 (pattern B, real unmodified upstream, main lever): a workspace recorded by an earlier run is replayed by exwsAllocate selectedRun: and reaches ExwsExecution.child(pathOnDisk) without ever passing the allocation check again; present unprotected in current upstream master
T2 (published-fix far site, real upstream): the value substituted into the disk-pool workspace pattern (test/${BRANCH} with BRANCH=../../outside) is expanded after the relative-path check
T3 (published-fix far site, real upstream): the controller browse endpoint serves a recorded pathOnDisk outside masterMountPoint
S1 (injected sibling): the cleanup action deletes a recorded workspace path outside masterMountPoint
S2 (injected sibling): the optional job-supplied sub-folder of the default path can contain '..'

S2 steps/ExwsAllocateStep.subPath + steps/ExwsAllocateExecution.computeSubPath: an optional @DataBoundSetter sub-folder appended to the default physicalPathOnDisk/$JOB_NAME/$BUILD_NUMBER path, validated only as a relative path
verified.services: none; everything runs offline after the image build
verified.project_tests_run: The plugin's own CustomWorkspaceTest (9 tests) and FormValidationUtilTest (10 tests) are compiled and run online during the environment image build with the Java 17 --add-opens flags the plugin's own argLine omits; both pass on the pinned+injected tree. The plugin's ExwsAllocateStepTest/ExwsStepTest are not used as a build gate because their disk-selection assertions pick a disk by the host filesystem's free space and are unstable in the container. Hidden suite: 8 security + 8 functional JenkinsRule tests; on the pinned+injected code all 8 security tests fail and all 8 functional tests pass, on the reference fix all 16 pass.
verified.coupled_behaviour: A relative nested custom path ('team/a/1'), a name that merely contains dots ('a..b/.cache'), a workspace pattern with ${JOB_NAME}/${BUILD_NUMBER} and a substituted nested value, a recorded allocation reused by a later build, a legitimate recorded workspace being browsed, a legitimate cleanup deleting only the workspace, and a legitimate sub-folder all keep working; an over-broad '..' substring rejection breaks the dotted-name case.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the value was produced by an earlier allocation, which the fix already validates, so this branch reads as a safe replay; the published fix never touches it and current upstream master still joins it unguarded
